ravi: FYI I hit a regression on multi-node 8xA100 runs this morning after landing the new kernel selection heuristics. End-to-end latency up ~18% for our TP/PP pipeline baseline. Profiling attached below. Anyone seen similar on mixed NVLink/PCIe racks?

julia: Can you paste the perf summary and config? Which NCCL alg and batch slicing are you using?

ravi: Quick paste from the flame/trace for a 6B model, tp=2 pp=4, global_batch=32, `auto` kernel selection: ```
allreduce (cross-node): 18.9ms avg (+52%)
allreduce (intra-node NVLink): 4.2ms
compute kernel (attn): 7.5ms
kv-cache lookup miss/hit ratio: 0.12 / 0.88
batching: continuous batching enabled, slice=256
CPU -> GPU transfer spikes seen on rank 3 when crossing PCIe
compute/comm overlap: reduced from ~20% to ~4%
```

kevin: Interesting — overlap collapse suggests the runtime is choosing kernels that increase latency variance (longer tail) which prevents effective asynchronous allreduce overlap. Mixed fabric probably amplifies it: NVLink ranks finish earlier, then cross-node ranks sit in queue waiting for PCIe/InfiniBand transfers. Could be KVCACHE coherence forcing barriers before KG read?

sam: Hypothesis: new kernel selection picks larger fused GEMM kernels to improve throughput on NVLink-heavy nodes, but the per-step variability increases on PCIe-bound nodes leading to more global allreduce stalls. Also worth checking whether the KV cache flush policy triggers cross-node sync earlier than before.

julia: Can you repro with `REDWOOD_KERNEL_FORCE=baseline` and `REDWOOD_BATCH_SLICE=128` to see if smaller kernels/shorter slices reduce tail? Also set `NCCL_LL_THRESHOLD=0` to force algorithm change for small messages.

ravi: Ran quick AB test: forcing baseline kernels + slice 128 brought latency back to -2% (i.e., slightly faster than pre-change). Forcing NCCL ring reduced cross-node allreduce to 13.2ms (vs 18.9ms). So two levers seem effective.

kevin: Good signal. Next steps: 1) add topology-aware kernel selection: prefer lower-variance kernels on nodes with slow PCIe links; 2) instrument KV cache coherence path to see if we call an explicit barrier on misses; 3) add a microbenchmark infra to sweep slice sizes x kernel variants across mixed racks.

infra-bot: perf trace uploaded: https://internal.redwood/prof/2623456789/trace.html (profile + NCCL traces).

sam: I'll own the microbench harness (PR draft https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1298). Kevin, can you add KV cache tracing logs (toggleable) so we can correlate misses with allreduce timings?

kevin: Yep will add `RV_KVCACHE_TRACE=1` flag and a shortlog with per-step sync points. Plan to run on perf cluster tomorrow morning (EFA vs IB vs PCIe-only nodes).

ravi: Thanks — owners and next steps clear. If the topology-aware kernel selection looks good we should gate the heuristics behind node topology detection for now.

julia: Agree. Also add a short doc note in /eng-runtime/runbooks about expected behavior and fallback knobs (`REDWOOD_KERNEL_*`, `REDWOOD_BATCH_SLICE`, `RV_KVCACHE_TRACE`).

sam: Will add runbook and results once microbench completes. :thumbsup:
